MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  POLICY DEVELOPMENT / STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION
  MARCH 10, 2020

An adjourned regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 3:04 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR
SCHMITZ.

1.  FLAG SALUTE

2.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development/Public Works Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Levi Sinkler
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

3.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  PRESENTATION BY AVENU INSIGHTS & ANALYTICS

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead introduced Fran Mancia and Laura Burnett of
  Avenu Insights & Analytics, who gave an update on the current state of the City’s Sales Tax,
  Property Taxes and Business Licenses, including:
  - Current Sales Tax Performance
  - Los Angeles County Pool: Internet Sales
  - AB147 and Online Sales Tax
  - Rolling Hills Estates’ Historical Sales Tax per Capita
  - Top 25 Businesses by Category
  - Sales Tax by Geographic Area
  - Quarter over Quarter Economic Performance
  - Sales Tax Trends & Forecast
  - Property Tax Allocation & Forecast
  Discussion ensued regarding the aging population, homes being inherited or
  sold, and the resulting effects on property taxes in the coming years.
  - Business License Administration Changes in 2019
  - Revenue Summary

4.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  MID-YEAR REPORTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file these reports.

  The Mid-Year status reports were presented for City Council consideration. City Manager
  Grammer noted that the reports are informational.

  Assistant City Manager Davis and Administrative Aide Sinkler summarized the City’s
  public outreach efforts over the last eight months including:
  - The first of two Community Roundup meetings

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
   -  Recognition of Rolling Hills Estates as Champions in the West Nile Virus
  Prevention Challenge by the County Board of Supervisors
  -  Tripepi Smith projects finalized including the “Welcome to RHE” booklet, the
  Peppertree Foundation logo, website banners, emergency preparedness card,
  a manure rate increase FAQ, and new public safety messenger
  -  Website Traffic and Statistics
  -  Social Media Insights and Top Posts
  -  Direct Messaging through Constant Contacts
  -  Enhancements to the website
  -  Nixle Alert and Notification System, soon to transition over to Alert South Bay
  -  Video library series completed by CGI highlighting Rolling Hills Estates

B.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION ITEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the items presented and prioritize them
  on the work plan for the coming fiscal year.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ requested to hear the Community Development & Public Works
  Director’s report first to accommodate the CPA consultant in attendance.

  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT & PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR

  CPA NON-RESIDENTIAL DEFAULT LEVEL

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), asking
  the Council to consider whether the Non-Residential default rate should remain at Lean
  Power (36% renewables) or be opted-up to match the Residential rate tier of 100% Green
  Power.

  Jennifer Ward, Director of External Affairs for the Clean Power Alliance, summarized the
  City’s current status and the options before them.

  Jennifer Ward responded to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s question, noting that the
  price difference between the Lean Power Level (36%) and Clean Power Level (50%) for
  commercial customers would be a difference of only 1%, while being significantly more
  renewable.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL confirmed that the Clean Power Level (50%) rate would
  be the same or less than what Southern California Edison would cost.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN stated that if the Council does choose to move forward
  with the change to the Clean Power Level, there would need to be effective and clear
  messaging to the customers being affected, explaining what options they have and how
  little it would cost to move from Lean to Clean.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN emphasized the importance of setting policy which
  affects climate action in a positive way.

  Discussion ensued regarding the options of staying at the current level or making the
  change to Clean.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  bring this item back to Council for further discussion, providing more details and
  data, as well as the messaging the City would employ.

  MALL SECURITY

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material). He summarized the proposed security ordinance, as well as the
  concerns of both the Promenade on the Peninsula and Chamber of Commerce, and
  asked Council for direction moving forward with an Ordinance or an agreement.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
   COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL summarized the events and issues that led to this item
  being brought to the Council.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated he supports an Ordinance to protect the safety
  of the community, and emphasized that it is the Council’s fundamental role to legislate on
  the topic of safety for the community.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL seconded COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s previous
  point. She then asked the City Attorney to confirm that any security plan would be exempt
  from the Public Records Act, which he confirmed and stated could be included into the
  Ordinance itself.

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba suggested creating a security
  plan before the Ordinance is adopted to work through the concerns of the shopping
  center.

  Public comment was received from the Chamber of Commerce in the form of a letter, and
  from Courtney Medak, Operations & Marketing Manager of Stoltz Management for the
  Promenade on the Peninsula, who spoke about their concerns and the ambiguity of the
  proposed Ordinance.

  Discussion ensued regarding the communication between the City, the Promenade and
  Chamber of Commerce, the specificity of the ordinance, and the Council’s responsibility
  to legislate.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct the City
  Attorney to discuss the Ordinance and concerns with the Promenade’s attorney
  and bring back a proposed Ordinance for the Council’s consideration at a future
  meeting.

  HOME SIZE AND LOT COVERAGE

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
  summarizing that there is no written policy setting home size, only a historical guideline
  of 5,000 sq. ft. maximum that has been used by planners and the Planning Commission
  over the years.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired if and why a set limit would need to be codified.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL stated that the guideline came about as part of
  Neighborhood Compatibility.

  City Attorney Davis stated that we can and do legislate on home size, using lot coverage
  ratio (30%). He suggested the Council adopt a guideline or policy rather than codifying a
  limit within the Ordinance.

  Discussion ensued regarding Neighborhood Compatibility, potential home sizes using lot
  coverage ratio, and the potential issues with the rigidity of setting a hard number limit
  versus a flexible guideline.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  draft guidelines with some flexibility and bring back to Council for consideration.

  ROOFING STANDARDS UPDATE

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that this report is an update for the Council (as per
  the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.
  PARKING REGULATIONS (OVERNIGHT IN COMMERCIAL DISTRICT)

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).
ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated there was no need to change the current
  process for the Commercial District.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to not make any
  changes to these regulations at this time.

  SIGN CODE UPDATES

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba stated that LED signage is
  required by code, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN’s question.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  NEW HOUSING AND ADU LAWS

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  This item is informational and will be brought back to the Council for a Public
  Hearing of an Urgency Ordinance and Regular Ordinance on March 24, 2020.

  RHNA ALLOCATION UPDATE

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  2020 CENSUS

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  OPEN SPACE

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that there has been a lot of interest and that the City
  has received two applications for Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) this year, in response
  to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN’s question.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN spoke about new housing legislation, ADUs and the
  importance of respecting your neighbors at a recent Homeowner’s Association (HOA)
  meeting.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ reported on her recent discussions at various HOA meetings.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  SUSTAINABILITY IN BUILDING STANDARDS

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material), summarizing that the Green Building Standard Code and Title 24
  puts the City in a good position with respect to sustainability.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
   This item is informational for the Council.

  STORM DRAIN IMPROVEMENTS

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material), stating that storm drain improvements have been completed at four
  locations on Palos Verdes Drive East, with Silver Spring Canyon at Hawthorne being the
  one outstanding project.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  STORM WATER PERMIT/SAFE CLEAN WATER PROGRAM (MEASURE W) UPDATE

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  City Manager Grammer clarified that the retrofit of the catch basins referenced refers to
  the installation of trash excluders to keep debris from entering the storm drain system.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  METROPOLITAN WATER DISTRICT (MWD) PROJECT UPDATE

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material), stating that the project has been delayed by a year and that the
  Metropolitan Water District (MWD) will compensate the City approximately $150,000 for
  the use of Butcher Park as a staging area.

  Discussion ensued about what should be done with the park in the interim.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to not leave the
  park empty.

  PUBLIC WORKS OPTIONS FOR SUSTAINABILITY

  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material), identifying what the City does with respect to sustainability in Public
  Works and potential grants that can be pursued.

  Discussion ensued about the benefits of rubberized asphalt.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  COMMUNITY SERVICES

  ARMENIAN GENOCIDE MEMORIAL (COUNCIL MEMBER FRANK ZERUNYAN)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN provided background on his service to the community
  and expressed gratitude to his colleagues and City staff. COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN proceeded to describe his vision for the Armenian Genocide Memorial which
  he sees as a parting gift to the City. He suggested the official dedication to take place on
  April 24, 2020 with a larger unveiling in December where dignitaries, various elected
  officials, and members of the Armenian community would attend.
  Public comment was provided by Vatche Shirikjian, who spoke about the birth of
  American philanthropy in the wake of the Armenian Genocide; he added that he sees the
  memorial as a way of thanking the United States.

  Council Members agreed that the memorial is a wonderful idea.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that the approximate cost of the memorial will
  be $20,000-$25,000, which will be collected through fundraising.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that the proposed location of the memorial will
  be reviewed by the Park & Activities Commission.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to send the
  proposal to the Park & Activities Commission for consideration at their meeting on
  March 16, 2020, and bring back to Council on April 14, 2020.

  UTILITY BOX ART PROJECT

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL and MAYOR SCHMITZ expressed their support of the
  program but would both like to have more information and details in order to make a more
  informed decision.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  bring this item back for consideration of the guidelines, budget and proposed
  process for this project.

  ROCKBLUFF PARK PLAY STRUCTURE

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), stating
  that staff expects to find a replacement play structure within the year which could be paid
  for using Park Facilities Fees.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  LANDSCAPE MEDIAN MASTER PLAN – PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
  explaining that staff aims to create a planting design guideline in order to maintain a
  consistent theme throughout the medians on Palos Verdes Drive North, west of Palos
  Verdes Drive East and east of Crenshaw Boulevard.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ asked about the previous agreement with Bennett Landscape to plant
  model medians. Discussion ensued about the work performed by Bennett Landscape and
  how the City arrived at the decision to proceed with the plan they did.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL suggested reaching out to South Coast Botanic Garden
  or the Land Conservancy for assistance.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested contacting resident Warren Arata, a
  landscape architect who is a member of the General Plan Advisory Committee.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  look at no-cost options discussed for design plans, and have Assistant City
  Manager Davis get a rough cost estimate from a professional for comparison, and
  bring back to Council for further discussion.

  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
  outlining the proposition of adding a fundraising arm to the Peppertree Foundation, and
  reexamining how the Peppertree Foundation supports City events.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
   Discussion ensued as to how a fundraising subcommittee would be formed and what
  projects they would raise money for. The group also discussed the changes that could be
  made to the Pepper Tree Foundation bylaws to support additional City events and
  projects.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  return with the current bylaws and proposed changes.

  ALLOCATION OF PARK FACILITIES FEES (ALSO KNOWN AS QUIMBY FUND)

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
  providing the City’s current Park Facilities Fee balance and what the City expects to
  collect over the next two years. She also provided an overview of select capital projects
  that could be funded with these fees.

  Discussion ensued as to the availability of grants to fund these projects. Council Members
  would like more information on grants prior to making any decisions about how Park
  Facilities Fees will be allocated. The consensus among the Council Members is that the
  Nature Center is a top priority.

  Assistant City Manager Davis and City Manager Grammer clarified that staff is actively
  seeking grants for the Nature Center.

  Discussion ensued about updates to the Council Chamber and City Hall, including the
  costs of the updates and how they could be partially funded by Park Facilities Fees.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

  PUBLIC SAFETY UPDATE

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) on
  the Flock Safety Camera Pilot Program.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated that the Montecillo neighborhood would like to request
  an extension of the Flock Camera Pilot Program due to Lomita Station’s initial lack of
  awareness of the technical features of the camera system.
  Discussion ensued about the Neighborhood Entryway Camera Grant Program.
  Administrative Analyst Slawson proposed that staff create a list of preferred vendors to
  allow the neighborhoods flexibility in their camera system choice.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  bring the program back for further discussion.

  EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
  summarizing emergency preparedness within the City’s equine community. Along with
  the Equine Emergency Preparedness Subcommittee, Administrative Analyst Slawson
  determined that, in the event of an emergency, water access would be the restricted for
  local horses and livestock. She went on to identify three possible locations for caches
  around the City.

  Discussion ensued about the possibility of using the reservoir in an emergency to the
  benefit of animals and residents.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  bring this item back to Council outlining various options.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
   YOUTH IN GOVERNMENT

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
  summarizing the proposed program.

  Discussion ensued regarding past participation in similar Youth in Government programs.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  return to Council with a formal outline of the program.

  PUBLIC OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  SENIOR COMMUNITY SUPPORT AND COLLABORATION

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
  explaining that staff has been meeting with Peninsula Seniors and the Palos Verdes
  Peninsula Village to determine how the City can strengthen its relationship with the senior
  community. Council’s direction is requested on whether the City should donate the $5,000
  requested by Peninsula Seniors to assist in extending their services to our senior
  community.

  Discussion ensued about how to address donation requests from local nonprofits.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested interested groups write a grant application
  to the City, outlining a project or service they could provide to the community, in which
  the City would donate.

  Assistant City Manager Davis suggested setting funds aside in the budget for community
  grants with established criteria, guidelines or policy.

  City Manager Grammer stated that potential recipients could apply for the grant annually
  for the Council’s consideration.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to
  bring back a policy and process for a grant program for the Council’s
  consideration.

  SOLID WASTE/RECYCLING UPDATES

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
  explaining the need for a future municipal code update due to laws recently passed.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN inquired about organic waste that is eventually
  composted.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ requested that Assistant City Manager Davis present her presentation
  shown to the Environmental Advisory Committee, to the Council and community.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported on new technology that will substantially
  improve organic waste recycling within two to five years.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER/CITY HALL RENOVATION

  City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
  the interior and exterior updates needed in the Council Chamber and City Hall.
ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
   Assistant City Manager Davis explained the scope of the project to be considered and
  provided background for each proposed update.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead went into further detail about work previously
  performed on the Council Chamber and City Hall and provided cost estimates on
  proposed updates.
  City Manager Grammer clarified that Park Facilities Funds can be used on Council
  Chamber renovations but that City Hall updates would not qualify.

  ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIRECTOR

  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  Discussion ensued regarding timing issues of payment reporting with the State Controller.

  This item is informational for the Council.

  FISCAL HEALTH REPORT, FY 2009-10 THROUGH FY 2018-19

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  COUNCILMEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE FISCAL HEALTH REPORT.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

  This item was received and filed by the Council.

  FINANCE UPDATE

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  This item is informational for the Council.

  INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY UPDATE

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  MAYOR SCHMITZ inquired about Torrance’s cyber-attack and Administrative Services
  Director Whitehead replied that Torrance has not yet released the cause.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead also provided an update on fiber installation
  and his intent to improve existing Wi-Fi at Ernie Howlett Park.

  This item is informational for the Council.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  9
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
 5.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:54 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular
  meeting of the City Council scheduled for Tuesday, March 24, 2020 at 7:00 p.m. in the
  Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  10
MARCH 10, 2020 (PDS)
